messages:
ryan p: Hey folks, new hire here on Fedora 38. Trying to run the repo with podman-compose. Postgres container exits during init with permission denied on the mounted ./pgdata dir. Anyone seen SELinux-related issues with DB mounts?

ryan p: Logs:
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: removing contents of data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
```

elaine (eng): welcome! :wave: Fedora + Podman + SELinux can definitely bite you. Podman uses different mount labeling than docker. Two quick options: 1) use a named volume (podman volume create ...) or 2) relabel the host path for container access with :z or :Z equivalent in podman, or change SELinux context temporarily.

sam infra: +1. With podman you can add `:Z` to the bind mount in compose to relabel, e.g. `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z`. If you prefer not to relabel host files, create a podman volume and copy data into it. Also check you're running the postgres image matching your arch.

ryan p: I tried `:Z` in the compose file and got an error from podman-compose that it doesn't understand `:Z`. Is there a podman-compose workaround?

elaine (eng): podman-compose sometimes lags docker-compose features. Workarounds: 1) switch to using a podman-native command to run the container and include `--security-opt label=type:container_file_t` or `--volume $(pwd)/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z` with podman run, or 2) use `chcon -R -t container_file_t pgdata/` on the host to set SELinux context yourself. Example: `sudo chcon -R -t container_file_t ./pgdata` then bring up compose.

sam infra: another approach: create a named volume and use a transient container to populate it from your host dir, which avoids SELinux relabeling:
```bash
podman volume create redwood_pgdata
podman run --rm -v redwood_pgdata:/to -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/from:ro alpine sh -c "cp -a /from/. /to/"
# then in compose use redwood_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

ryan p: thanks. I tried chcon and that worked 1 postgres started. But our CLI scripts expect to run host psql for resets and they still fail because they assume a host DB socket. Any recommended pattern for podman?

elaine (eng): same pattern as Docker: run db CLI in the container or run a short-lived psql podman container on the same network. e.g.: `podman exec -it <postgres-container> psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"` or `podman run --rm --network container:<postgres-container> -e PGPASSWORD=localpass postgres:15 psql -h localhost -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"`. We avoid host-level DB file ops for containerized DBs.

setup-bot: Dev docs (internal): https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local (note: podman tips added) :link:

ryan p: great, chcon + running psql in-container fixed my flow. I'll add a note to my onboarding checklist about Fedora/podman/SELinux gotchas and the chcon trick. Thanks everyone! :tada:
